skill.name: task-runner
skill.description: Run project commands through the just task runner. The skill helps discover justfile recipes and execute common tasks such as tests, builds, linting, and development commands.
skill.summary: Discover and run project justfile tasks for tests, builds, linting, and local workflows.
skill.author: 0xDarkMatter

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally invokes the external just CLI and project-defined recipes through Bash. Most static findings are real command-execution surfaces, while several markdown fence matches are false positives. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found, but the skill should avoid treating bare just as a safe discovery command.

remediation.issue: Bare just is presented as a discovery command.
remediation.suggestion: Use just --list or just --summary for discovery, then run a named recipe only after user confirmation.

remediation.issue: Project recipes can execute arbitrary shell commands.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users that recipes inherit local permissions and may run scripts, remove files, or contact deployment systems.

remediation.issue: Destructive and deployment recipes appear in examples.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before running clean, deploy, production, or custom recipes with external side effects.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 17 instructs using the external just CLI for recipe discovery. This is a real command-execution surface because bare just can run project-defined behavior instead of only listing recipes.
Line 18 recommends running just test, which executes a project-defined recipe through the shell. This is expected for the skill but still depends on untrusted repository task definitions.

The block beginning at line 24 shows runnable just commands, including test, build, lint, deploy, and a specific justfile path. These commands execute project-controlled recipes and can have side effects.
The matched range starts on a markdown code-fence delimiter rather than an executable command. Adjacent command examples are covered by other findings.

The justfile example includes shell commands for tests, builds, linting, dev servers, cleanup, and deployment. These are executable recipe bodies and demonstrate that task execution can modify files or trigger external systems.
The matched text is a markdown fence boundary between sections. It does not itself instruct execution of a command.

The discovery block beginning at line 73 contains just --summary, just --show, and just --list commands. They are lower-risk than recipe execution but still invoke an external CLI against project files.
The match starts on a markdown closing fence and does not directly represent command execution. The later bullet that contains just is evaluated in its own finding.
Line 86 tells the agent to run bare just first in a new project. That can execute a default recipe from the repository, so it is a real unexpected command-execution risk.
Line 87 recommends just test, which runs a repository-defined recipe. The command is legitimate for the skill but can execute arbitrary shell chosen by the project.
Line 88 recommends just build and the surrounding section allows any project-specific task. This delegates execution to project-defined recipes with local filesystem and environment access.
The code block at lines 95-97 invokes just --list for discovery. It is a legitimate lower-risk command, but it still runs an external CLI in the project context.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Discovery Command May Run Default Recipe
semantic_findings.description: The skill labels bare just as a way to list recipes in multiple places. In many just projects, invoking just without an explicit listing flag can run the default recipe, causing command execution when the user expected discovery.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file repeatedly presents no-argument just as discovery while also showing safer just --list usage later. This is a behavior-level risk distinct from the markdown backtick matches.

content.value_statement: Project commands are often hidden across scripts and documentation. This skill finds justfile recipes and runs selected tasks through Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether a project uses a justfile for task automation.
Lists available just recipes with just --summary or just --list.
Runs common recipes such as test, build, lint, and dev.
Shows details for a specific recipe with just --show.
Runs recipes from a selected justfile path when requested.
Passes explicit arguments to just recipes when the user requests them.
limitations: Requires the just CLI to be installed in the environment.
Only works when a repository provides a justfile or compatible recipe file.
Recipes can execute arbitrary shell commands defined by the project.
Does not prove that deploy, clean, or custom recipes are safe before execution.

use_cases.title: Run Local Checks
use_cases.description: List available recipes, then run project tests, builds, or lint tasks from the justfile.

use_cases.title: Inspect Automation Commands
use_cases.description: Review available just recipes before changing continuous integration or release workflows.

use_cases.title: Validate Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Find the repository's standard verification commands and run the relevant checks during review.

prompt_templates.title: List Available Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this project for a justfile and list the available recipes without running a task.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner discovery in a new repository

prompt_templates.title: Run Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the test recipe in the justfile, show what it will run, then execute it if it looks safe.

prompt_templates.title: Build and Lint
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the build and lint recipes, explain any side effects, then run the safe local checks.

prompt_templates.title: Run Targeted Recipe
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the backend justfile, inspect the named recipe, and run it with the environment argument after confirmation.

output_examples.input: List the available just tasks for this project.
output_examples.output: The project has recipes for tests, builds, linting, development, cleanup, and deployment. I would run only listing commands unless you choose a recipe.
The test recipe is a local verification task. I inspected it, ran it, and will report the command result and any failures.

output_examples.input: Can you deploy production with just?
output_examples.output: A deployment recipe exists, but it can affect external systems. I will describe the recipe and wait for explicit confirmation before running it.

best_practices: List recipes before running any task in a new repository.
Ask for confirmation before deploy, clean, or other destructive recipes.
Run narrow tasks first, then broader build or test tasks when needed.
anti_patterns: Running deploy or clean recipes without explaining the impact.
Assuming every project uses just when no justfile exists.
Passing unreviewed user arguments into recipes that touch production systems.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps discover and run project tasks defined in a justfile.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require just to be installed?
faq.answer: Yes. The environment must have the just CLI available.

faq.question: Can it run tests and builds?
faq.answer: Yes. It can run test, build, lint, dev, and other recipes that the project defines.

faq.question: Is it safe to run every recipe?
faq.answer: No. Recipes can run arbitrary shell commands, so risky tasks should be inspected first.

faq.question: Can it work in subdirectories?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes examples for selecting a justfile from a subdirectory.
